# Monitor measurements (device layer)

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

The monitor's measurement chain: how the simulated monitor turns the patient's signals into the numbers a clinician
reads — ECG filtering and QRS detection, heart rate, SpO2, oscillometric NIBP, invasive pressure numerics, pulse
detection, CO2 numerics, impedance respiration, temperature, the 12-lead capture, trends and the event log. Every
numeric is measured from the displayed waveform or a device model, never copied from the physiological truth, so delays,
artefacts and failed measurements behave as they do at the bedside. For an embedding developer this is part of the
device layer the engine keeps beside its physiology (`l3/device-layer.ts`).
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- ECG filters: monitor mode 0.5–40 Hz with an automatic mains notch (50 Hz by default), diagnostic mode 0.05–150 Hz
  without a notch; Butterworth sections from Bristow-Johnson's biquad cookbook, notch Q 8 (`l3/ecg-filter.ts`;
  research 03 §1.11).
- QRS detection on the displayed lead, Pan–Tompkins-like: 5–15 Hz band-pass, derivative, squaring, 80 ms moving
  integral, adaptive threshold NPK + 0.25·(SPK − NPK) with a 200 ms refractory period; a small hump within 600 ms of the
  last R is taken as a T wave (Pan & Tompkins 1985; `l3/qrs.ts`).
- Heart rate: mean of the last 12 RR intervals without the largest and smallest (or the plain mean, per skin), the last
  4 when the last 3 exceed 1200 ms, and 0 after 4 s without a QRS (`l3/hr.ts`; research 03 §1.12).
- SpO2: site SaO2 after the circulatory delay, a first-order sensor lag (τ 3 s), device bias, a moving average (8 s by
  default; the skin may set another) and a display update; validity comes from the pleth (`l3/spo2/spo2.ts`;
  research 03 §3.6–3.7). The pulse-tone pitch is 880·2^(−(100 − SpO2)·s/12) Hz (`l3/spo2/spo2.ts`).
- NIBP: inflate to 165 mmHg, deflate in 8 mmHg steps; each pulse's oscillation is A(Pc) = Amax·exp(−((Pc − MAP)/w)²)
  with Amax = 4·tanh(PP/50); MAP is the envelope peak and SBP/DBP are read where the envelope falls to 0.50/0.80 of it,
  plus 4 mmHg noise; a weak envelope or SBP < 50 fails the attempt (`l3/nibp/nibp.ts`; research 03 §5).
- Invasive pressures: per beat, SBP/DBP are the maximum/minimum of the displayed waveform between two feet and MAP is
  the beat's integral; values are averaged over the last 6 fresh beats and shown at 1 Hz; a line with fewer than 2 beats
  of ≥ 3 mmHg at ≥ 25/min is non-pulsatile (`l3/pressure-numerics/numerics.ts`; research/05 §6).
- CO2: a breath is a rising edge above 50 % of the recent peak; EtCO2 is the highest breath peak of the last 10 s,
  FiCO2 the inspiratory minimum, awRR the mean of 6 intervals; gas apnoea after 20 s (`l3/co2-numerics/co2-numerics.ts`;
  research 03 §4.5).
- Impedance respiration is chest volume plus a cardiogenic ripple (10 % of a 500 mL breath) with an adaptive-threshold
  detector, so ripple can be counted as breaths when breathing is shallow (`l3/resp/impedance.ts`; research 03 §7).
- Temperature probes add a first-order lag under 10 s at 0.1 °C resolution (`l3/temp/temp-numerics.ts`); trends keep
  each numeric at 1 Hz for 8 h (`l3/trends/trend-store.ts`); the 12-lead capture takes the last 10 s through the
  diagnostic filter (`l3/capture12/capture.ts`; research/05 §2.6).
<!-- /hand:equations -->

### [`l3/pulse/detector.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/src/l3/pulse/detector.ts)

| Name | Value | Unit | Source / tag | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DET_RATE` | `125` | — | Pulse; brief §4.2; research 03 §2.2; Zong et al. 2003 | Pulse (upstroke) detector for ABP, PAP and pleth (brief §4.2 "PR from the ABP uses slope-sum upstroke detection"; research 03 §2.2). Slope-sum function after Zong et al. 2003 (written from the paper's description): SSF(n) = Σ_{k=n−w+1..n} max(0, x_k − x_{k−1}), w = 128 ms. A pulse is an upward crossing of an adaptive threshold (35% of the running SSF-peak average, never below a per-channel floor) outside a 250 ms refractory period; its foot is the minimum of the signal in the 128 ms before the crossing. Scale-free, so it works on mmHg (ABP/PAP) and on PI units (pleth). All state is plain data. |
